proposals.statement:
theorem leftDiagonal_onset_le_not_of_black_ladder :
    ¬ ∃ N : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ k, N k < N (k + 1)) ∧ (∀ k, N k ≤ k) ∧
      (∀ k, leftDiagonal (k + 1) (N (k + 1)) = true ∨
        (∀ j ≥ N k + 1, leftDiagonal (k + 1) j = false)) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: The onset wall's own description tells the next attempt where to go: 'Decompose before attempting again: leftDiagonal_onset_le_of_black_ladder reduces it to one sequence of black-cell witnesses.' That route is dead, and this node is the proof of it. The closed block's ladder is strictly increasing, so N k ≥ N 0 + k ≥ k; the wall needs N k ≤ k; so N k = k is the only admissible ladder, and there is no freedom left anywhere. At k = 2 the block's witness hypothesis then asks that diagonal 3 be black at index 3, or white from index 3 on. Diagonal 3 alternates with index parity — evolve_left_fourth_diagonal, closed — so it is white at 3 and black at 4, and both branches fail. Not a technicality at one index: measured over the forced ladder, the black witness fails at 1514 of the 3001 indices k ≤ 3000, and the eventually-white escape covers exactly four of them (k = 1, 6, 27, 398, i.e. the eventually-white diagonals 2, 7, 28, 399), leaving 1510 failures with no branch at all. Measured twice in two implementations: explorer/seeder_ladder.mjs in the packed-row model (cross-checked against A051023, against explorer/rule30.mjs, and against the three proved edge diagonals), and in Lean on the real definition, where `(List.range 8).all fun k => leftDiagonal (k+1) (k+1)` evaluates to false. A proof of leftDiagonal_onset_le cites this by not spending a thirteenth attempt on the route the board currently recommends — twelve attempts and $51.80 have gone into that wall — and by moving to the packed-row front, which the other three nodes of this tier supply.
proposals.disclaims: Does not say leftDiagonal_onset_le_of_black_ladder is useless. It says only that the block cannot yield the wall's `∃ N ≤ k` directly, because its conclusion's onset IS the ladder's own N k; a proof that uses the block and then improves the onset by other means is untouched. It says nothing about whether the wall is true — the measured onsets are at most k/2 for every k ≤ 722 and the wall is believed. It bears on no prize conjecture: this is the left edge of the cone, where periodicity is already proved.

route.tactics:
rintro ⟨N, hmono, hle, hwit⟩
  have hge : ∀ k, k ≤ N k := by
    intro k
    induction k with
    | zero => exact Nat.zero_le _
    | succ k ih => have := hmono k; omega
  have hEq : ∀ k, N k = k := fun k => le_antisymm (hle k) (hge k)
  have h3 : leftDiagonal 3 3 = false := by
    have := evolve_left_fourth_diagonal 3
    simpa [leftDiagonal] using this
  have h4 : leftDiagonal 3 4 = true := by
    have := evolve_left_fourth_diagonal 4
    simpa [leftDiagonal] using this
  rcases hwit 2 with h | h
  · rw [hEq 3, h3] at h
    exact absurd h (by simp)
  · have h5 := h 4 (by rw [hEq 2]; omega)
    rw [h4] at h5
    exact absurd h5 (by simp)

proposals.statement:
theorem leftDiagonal_periodicFrom_of_rowNat_agree (k p T : ℕ) (hT : T ≤ 2 * k)
    (h : rowNat T % 2 ^ (k + 1) = rowNat (T + p) % 2 ^ (k + 1)) :
    PeriodicFrom (leftDiagonal k) p k := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: The onset wall in one congruence per diagonal, and the interface every packed-row attempt on it wants. Diagonal k at index j is bit k of the packed row j + k (leftDiagonal_eq_rowNat_testBit, closed), so 'diagonal k has settled by index k' asks exactly that rows T and T + p agree on bit k for every T ≥ 2k. Agreement on the low k+1 bits at one time T ≤ 2k is enough, because the low bits are autonomous — see rowNat_agree_forward in this tier — and bit k depends on nothing above the residue mod 2^(k+1). Why a proof of the wall cites it: the wall follows in three lines by choosing T and p per k, checked as an `example` in explorer/seeder_scratch_front.lean, and this form is strictly freer than either closed reduction. leftDiagonal_onset_le_iff_rowNat_return pins T = 2k and p = 2^k; leftDiagonal_onset_le_of_stepMod_preperiod demands the preperiod bound for EVERY start x < 2^(k+1) when only the orbit of 1 is the seed's row. Here T and p are the prover's to choose. It is also the shape leftDiagonal_onset_le_of_le_5000 actually used to reach depth 5000 on the single shift 16, stated once so the next attempt does not rebuild it a fifth time.
proposals.disclaims: Says nothing about whether such a congruence exists at large k; that is the wall itself, and what remains after this node is a lower bound on where the width-(k+1) truncated orbit of 1 first returns. The shift p must be allowed to vary with k and this statement does: no single p serves every k, because leftDiagonal_period_unbounded is proved and crystal 57 gives each uniform constant's exact expiry (16 dies at k = 87867). Not a prize conjecture; the left edge only.

route.tactics:
have fwd : ∀ t, T ≤ t → rowNat t % 2 ^ (k + 1) = rowNat (t + p) % 2 ^ (k + 1) := by
    intro t hTt
    obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hTt
    subst hd
    simp only [rowNat_mod_eq_iterate] at h ⊢
    have e1 : T + d = d + T := by omega
    have e2 : T + d + p = d + (T + p) := by omega
    rw [e2, e1, Function.iterate_add_apply, Function.iterate_add_apply, h]
  intro n hn
  rw [leftDiagonal_eq_rowNat_testBit, leftDiagonal_eq_rowNat_testBit]
  have hag := fwd (n + k) (by omega)
  have key : ∀ m : ℕ, (rowNat m).testBit k = (rowNat m % 2 ^ (k + 1)).testBit k := by
    intro m; rw [Nat.testBit_mod_two_pow]; simp
  rw [show n + p + k = n + k + p from by omega, key (n + k + p), key (n + k), hag]

witness.range: k < 7, T ≤ 2k, p < 9, conclusion read at 12 successive indices — entirely in the packed row model, so no 3^t cost and no depth wall

proposals.statement:
theorem rowNat_agree_forward (n T p t : ℕ) (hTt : T ≤ t)
    (h : rowNat T % 2 ^ n = rowNat (T + p) % 2 ^ n) :
    rowNat t % 2 ^ n = rowNat (t + p) % 2 ^ n := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: The low bits of a row are autonomous, so an agreement between two rows can never be lost. Bit b of row t+1 reads only bits b, b-1, b-2 of row t, so truncating to the low n bits commutes with the step; two rows agreeing there agree there for ever after. Three lines from the closed rowNat_mod_eq_iterate: the truncated rows are the orbit of 1 under stepMod n, so if two orbit points coincide at T, applying the map t − T more times keeps them coincident. Harvest rather than invention, and this is the argument for the node: it has now been re-proved privately three times, in three different sessions, under three names — the 'one autonomy induction' inside leftDiagonal_onset_le_iff_rowNat_return, `iterate_eq_of_eq` inside leftDiagonal_onset_le_of_le_5000, and part of `agree_bdry` inside the walk parked by onset attempts 11 and 12. It is the same case periodicFrom_trans_period was seeded on. Any proof of leftDiagonal_onset_le through the packed row cites it, because it is the only reason an agreement front is monotone in time, and monotone is what lets a front reach height k+1 by row 2k.
proposals.disclaims: Pure bookkeeping about a deterministic map on finitely many states; there is no automaton content and no bound on anything. It says agreement is never lost, not that it is ever gained — gaining a bit is rowNat_return_succ_iff, already closed, and how often that succeeds is the wall.

route.tactics:
obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hTt
  subst hd
  simp only [rowNat_mod_eq_iterate] at h ⊢
  have e1 : T + d = d + T := by omega
  have e2 : T + d + p = d + (T + p) := by omega
  rw [e2, e1, Function.iterate_add_apply, Function.iterate_add_apply, h]

witness.expression: (List.range 30).all fun T => (List.range 6).all fun n => (List.range 6).all fun p => (List.range 10).all fun d => !(decide (rowNat T % 2 ^ n = rowNat (T + p) % 2 ^ n)) || decide (rowNat (T + d) % 2 ^ n = rowNat (T + d + p) % 2 ^ n)
witness.range: T < 30, n < 6, p < 6, d < 10 — 10,800 instances of the implication, in the packed row model, so no 3^t cost

proposals.statement:
theorem rowNat_testBit_zero (t : ℕ) : (rowNat t).testBit 0 = true := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: The left edge of the cone, said in the packed row model: the lowest bit of every row is set, so every row is an odd number. leftDiagonal 0 is the left edge and is black at every index (evolve_left_edge, closed), and leftDiagonal 0 t is bit 0 of row t (leftDiagonal_eq_rowNat_testBit, closed), so this is those two composed and nothing else. Why an onset proof cites it: it is the base case of every front argument on the packed rows. A front starts at height 1 precisely because any two rows agree on their lowest bit, and the walk parked by attempts 11 and 12 had to prove this privately (as rowNat_testBit_zero, then again as `agree_one`) before it could take its first step. It also records why the halving law does not apply to the seed's own orbit: step_two_mul makes the even states a copy of the whole system one bit narrower, and this says rowNat never enters them.
proposals.disclaims: Supply, not insight — a change of notation for a fact the board closed long ago, provable in three lines from two closed nodes. It bears on no prize conjecture, and it gives no bound on any onset or period.

route.tactics:
have h : leftDiagonal 0 t = true := evolve_left_edge t
  rw [leftDiagonal_eq_rowNat_testBit] at h
  simpa using h

witness.range: t < 300 — packed row model, no 3^t cost
